name: The Franco Company
old_description: The Franco Company is a custom furnishing company. We provide made to order pieces of furniture and Art. Our products are hand made in Dallas, TX. We take pride in working providing custom detail to each of our clients and enjoy the one on one interactions with them to create the perfect design.
about:
Founded in 2015 and based in Rowlett, Texas, The Franco Company operates as a custom furnishing business producing made-to-order furniture and art. The company's workshop is located in the Dallas area, where each piece is handcrafted to client specifications.

The company specializes in custom handcrafted furniture, millwork, conference tables, and reception desks for both residential and commercial settings. Materials include solid wood, exotic veneers, high-end laminates, and steel, combined with modern fabrication technology. Every product is built to individual requirements, from statement coffee tables to collaborative workspace solutions.

Clients span commercial offices, hospitality venues, and interior design firms. Notable commercial projects include the American Airlines Center, AT&T Discovery District, and Marriott Hotels. Design-firm partners include Erin Sander Design, Marly & Co, SJL Design, Angeline Guido Design, and Autumn Cooper Design. Local hospitality accounts feature Lochlands Irish Pub, Revolving Kitchen, Fortunate Sons, and Recess Dallas.

The Franco Company emphasizes its use of premium materials and current technology as differentiators, stating that solid wood, exotic veneers, high-end laminates, and real steel set its work apart. The firm also highlights one-on-one client collaboration to ensure each piece reflects the customer's unique needs.

name: The Plastics Group of America
old_description: Offering custom compounding to meet customer’s needs since 1973
about:
The Plastics Group of America (TPG) is headquartered in Woonsocket, Rhode Island, where it was founded in 1973 by Bob Lebeaux as Ralco Industries, a one-man scrap trading operation. The company remains family-owned, with second-generation leadership including President and CEO Marti Lebeaux and Executive Vice President Michael Rosenthal, who joined in 1979. The business adopted its current name in 1988 after merging Ralco, the Polifil® compounding line, and the Transcontinental Polymers recycling unit.

TPG operates over 300,000 square feet of manufacturing space in Woonsocket and runs a 24/7 production schedule. Its core business is custom compounding of Polifil® polypropylene-based reinforced resins, using mineral, talc, calcium, glass, and barium additives to meet specific physical, mechanical, and thermal requirements. An on-site quality control laboratory equipped with melt index, Izod, flexural, tensile, DSC, moisture, ash, Gardner impact, and color testing instruments certifies every batch, whether the order is 100 pounds or one million pounds. The company also provides recycling and toll processing services, densifying, guillotining, and extruding scrap into reusable material, and acts as a resin broker and distributor with stocking points across the continental United States.

The compounded resins serve processors in appliance, automotive, construction, consumer housewares and disposables, furniture, industrial/institutional/electronic, medical and personal care, packaging, and pump/pool/spa/irrigation markets. TPG's ISO 9001-certified facility supplies molders, extruders, and blow-molding operations that require consistent, specification-grade thermoplastics.

TPG emphasizes its asset-based manufacturing model combined with a full-service approach: free commercial color matching, technical consulting through its TPGOA Technical Insights library, and a commitment to on-time, on-budget delivery. The company traces its differentiation to the 1980 launch of custom compounding under the Polifil® brand and its early adoption of ISO 9002 certification in 1996, followed by an OSHA SHARP award in 1997.

name: The Tri-M Group, LLC
old_description: The Tri-M Group specializes in the design, installation and service of high voltage, electrical construction, building automation systems, data and telecommunications networks, security and energy analytics.
about:
The Tri-M Group, LLC is headquartered in Kennett Square, Pennsylvania, with additional offices in Lock Haven, Quakertown, Middletown (Delaware), and Baltimore (Maryland). The company was founded in 1964 by brothers Tom and Dick Musser as a small industrial and commercial electrical contractor.

Today Tri-M employs over 500 people and provides design, installation, and ongoing service for high-voltage electrical construction, building automation systems, data and telecommunications networks, security solutions, and energy analytics. The company operates a panel fabrication shop and offers 24/7/365 emergency and scheduled maintenance, remote engineering support, and a proprietary online project tracking tool called ProNav.

Tri-M serves industrial and commercial clients across the Mid-Atlantic region, including facilities that require energy benchmarking, building automation upgrades, secure network infrastructure, and high-voltage electrical work. Its customer base spans manufacturing plants, commercial buildings, institutional campuses, and utility projects.

The firm emphasizes a culture rooted in safety, ethical decision-making, collaborative problem-solving, and superior service delivery. Leadership states that the ESOP structure was chosen to preserve the company’s independence, retain its workforce, and continue the legacy of founder Tom Musser, who believed in giving back to the community and empowering employees.

name: The Wooden Nickel - Custom Live Edge Furniture
old_description: Every once in a while a project comes through the shop that reminds us why we started building furniture in the first place. This past spring, a family from Marshall County asked for a live edge dining table big enough to hold three generations at once. They...
about:
Based in Arab, Alabama, The Wooden Nickel builds custom live edge furniture from locally sourced hardwood slabs. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed; it operates as a shop where each piece begins with a slab selected for its natural character.

The shop produces dining tables, desks, adjustable workstations, and contract-grade furniture for commercial spaces. The process is deliberately slow: logs from tree services and loggers are kiln-dried and stabilized, then flattened, sanded, and inspected for cracks or knots that may receive resin filling. Finishes are applied in multiple hand-rubbed coats, and steel bases—fabricated from high-tolerance steel—are fitted to ensure level, wobble-free assembly. The company notes that most production is custom, ranging from single items to larger commercial orders.

Customers include residential clients such as a Marshall County family that commissioned a three-generation dining table, as well as local businesses needing tables and work surfaces for offices, break rooms, and public areas. The firm has supplied several area companies with thicker slabs, reinforced bases, and durable finishes designed for daily wear.

The Wooden Nickel emphasizes careful material selection, honest construction, and an unhurried timeline. As the owners describe it, the goal is furniture that 'doesn't draw attention to itself' but 'just keeps working year after year'—built to be used, built to last, and built for real life.

Steel bases fabricated in-house from high-tolerance steel
Logs sourced from local tree services and loggers
No templates or shortcuts; each slab unique
Contract-grade durability for commercial use

old_description: Located just two blocks north of L.L.Bean’s flagship store, our flagship showroom is a convenient and picturesque stop if you visit Maine. We restored a nineteenth-century home and furnished two full floors with classic and new Thos. Moser furniture designs and Maine artwork. about:
Thos. Moser’s Freeport showroom occupies a restored nineteenth-century home in Freeport, Maine, two blocks north of L.L.Bean’s flagship store. The company has not disclosed the showroom’s opening year or its ownership structure, and no founders are named in connection with this location.

The showroom spans two full floors displaying classic and current Thos. Moser furniture designs alongside Maine artwork. An attached carriage house functions as an outlet annex where unique pieces are available for immediate purchase. The location operates Monday through Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday noon–5 p.m., and offers scheduled consultations for standard and custom furniture designs through its Customer in Residence (CIR) program, managed by Steve Wyman.

The showroom serves visitors to Maine as well as residential and commercial buyers seeking handmade wooden furniture. The product lineup includes commercial products, and the CIR program caters to clients exploring custom designs. The space also hosts art exhibitions, such as the “Dedicated to Art” display running through October 31, 2026, pairing paintings and prints with furniture.

The company positions the Freeport location as a flagship destination that blends retail with an immersive experience, emphasizing the historic setting, immediate availability of outlet pieces, and personalized consultation services as differentiators.
